title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity, from procurement reorganizations in the Space Force to ambitious funding rounds for emerging tech. As companies jockey for position in an increasingly crowded market, the stakes are high, and the volatility is palpable.

themes.title: Space Force's New Structure
themes.body: The Space Force has completed a significant procurement reorganization, establishing nine distinct acquisition portfolios. This move aims to streamline operations and enhance efficiency, but it also raises questions about how effectively these portfolios will adapt to rapid technological changes.

themes.title: Funding for Laser Tech
themes.body: Pulse Space's $40 million award from the Space Force underscores a growing interest in advanced power technologies, particularly laser systems. As the military leans into these capabilities, we can expect a flurry of innovation, though the path from funding to functional tech remains fraught with challenges.

themes.title: Hypersonic Delays Persist
themes.body: The ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing highlight the complexities of developing cutting-edge defense technologies. With this being the third consecutive quarter of setbacks, stakeholders are left wondering if the promised capabilities will ever materialize.

themes.title: Market Dynamics Shift
themes.body: The recent surge in funding rounds, such as True Anomaly's $190 million Series C, reflects a shifting landscape where capital is flowing into space startups. However, with the Defense-Tech IPO window cracking open, the competition for investor attention is likely to intensify.
